source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 9 декабря ст. ст. — «Свт. Софрония, архиеп. Кипрского (VI).»

attestations.note: The Russian calendar keeps him ONE DAY LATER IN THE MENOLOGION than the Romanian and Greek rows above, 9 декабря against their 8 December, and the difference is neither the thirteen days of the style conversion nor a second feast in one calendar: it is two churches numbering the same commemoration differently. The reading at /Life/life3091.htm is the Greek one in every particular it touches — the Christian family on Cyprus, the learning, the gift of wonders, the election to the see of a dead bishop by the will of the whole people — so this is the same man and not a second Sophronius. The line calls him «архиеп.», archbishop, where the Romanian and Greek lines say bishop; THE FOLDER’S OFFICE IS LEFT AT `Bishop of Cyprus` and the disagreement is not resolved here. The line closes «(VI)», the only century any of the three calendars gives, and the folder’s `dates` are written from it. The day page prints seven hymns and none is under his name.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 8 decembrie — «Sfântul Ierarh Sofronie, Episcopul Ciprului»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 8ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Όσιος Σωφρόνιος επίσκοπος Κύπρου»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 8 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man: the Cypriot of devout Christian parents who was chosen for the see after the death of the bishop Damianos. The day's line calls him «επίσκοπος Κύπρου» while the text says he became «Αρχιεπίσκοπος Κύπρου»; the folder's existing office, Bishop of Cyprus, is left as it stands and the page's own second word is recorded here rather than written into the field. It gives no year, so the folder's dateless state stands. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (25 September 2026).

death.note: From the Roman numeral the Russian day line closes with, «(VI)»; neither the Romanian nor the Greek calendar gives a century, and the life page gives no year at all.
